articles.title: SJAA EPHEMERIS
articles.summary: This document is the "SJAA Ephemeris," the official publication of the San Jose Astronomical Association for March 1996. It represents Volume 7, Number 3 of their club's newsletter.

articles.title: Eye on the Universe
articles.summary: The article details recent Board of Directors elections for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) and announces the 16th Annual Bay Area Astronomical Auction and Swap Meet scheduled for May 4, featuring a capped commission. It also provides a comprehensive calendar of club events for March and April 1996, including general meetings, star parties at various locations, and astronomy workshops, alongside information on other regional astronomical conferences.

articles.title: What to Expect for Comet C/1996 B2 Hyakutake
articles.summary: Comet C/1996 B2 Hyakutake was visually discovered on January 31, 1996, and is projected to become a very bright, potentially 1st magnitude object in March, April, and May of 1996. Observers in the Northern Hemisphere are particularly favored in late March, as the comet will make a close approach to Earth (0.10 AU) on March 25 and become circumpolar, though it is expected to appear as a large, diffuse object.

articles.title: Mark Wagner
articles.summary: Mark Wagner details a highly successful astronomy observing trip to Fremont Peak, despite initial conflicting weather forecasts. The night offered exceptional clear and dry conditions, allowing him to hunt Herschel objects, bagging 28, and enjoy spectacular views of Messier objects. Highlights included M42 through a high-quality refractor with bino-viewers and the Horsehead Nebula with a UHC filter, making up for previous poor observing conditions.

articles.title: Where Was Everybody? Star Party at Henry Coe, January 13, 1996
articles.summary: Gary Mitchell recounts attending a star party at Henry Coe State Park on January 13, 1996, with his mother, expecting a large turnout due to favorable weather and dark sky conditions. To his surprise, he was the only club member who showed up, though several visitors came hoping to learn about the club. Despite the low club member presence, the group enjoyed an exceptional evening of observing with very dark skies and steady seeing, viewing objects like the Orion Nebula and various deep-sky objects.

articles.title: Clear Skies, Hot Photons, Cool CCDs
articles.summary: At a February general meeting, experienced astro-photographers Brian Drummond and Benoit Shillings shared their insights into CCD astro-photography. Drummond showcased the Barry CCD Kit's ease of use and impressive results, while Shillings detailed his experiences with the Kit and the ST-7 camera, including unique image processing techniques. Their presentations left many attendees interested in exploring CCD technology themselves.

articles.title: The Public May Participate!
articles.summary: NASA's Mars Global Surveyor (MGS), set to launch in November 1996, will carry a Mars Relay system for communication with future Mars landers. JPL plans a near-Earth test of this relay approximately 20-30 days after launch, inviting student and amateur radio operators to participate. Using 70 cm antennas, individuals can listen for a 1.3-watt beacon from the MGS spacecraft on 437.1 MHz, providing a unique "ultimate DX" opportunity.

articles.title: Hyakutake, continued from page 1
articles.summary: This article details the expected appearance of Comet Hyakutake (C/1996 B2) as it approaches Earth and perihelion. It discusses the challenges and possibilities of observing its tail due to foreshortening, varying distances, and dust production, particularly noting that a long, faint tail might be visible to experienced observers under dark skies between March 22-31. The text also provides brightness estimates and differentiates between pre-perihelion views (Northern Hemisphere) and post-perihelion views (Southern Hemisphere), which will see a rapidly fading comet.

articles.title: Ephemerides for C1996 B2 Hyakutake at closest approach to Earth. These Ephemerides are based on data available as of Feb 12. Notice that there is already discrepancy with Don Machholtz's Ephemerides that are dated Feb 9. Expect more revisions as the comet gets closer. (Distances are in AU.)
articles.summary: This document provides updated ephemerides for Comet C1996 B2 Hyakutake, detailing its position, distance, and magnitude during its closest approach to Earth in March. It highlights a discrepancy with earlier ephemerides and advises expecting further revisions as the comet nears. The data is current as of February 12th, 1996.

articles.title: Periodical Publication Statement
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) publishes its monthly newsletter, "SJAA Ephemeris," 12 times a year from January through December. Members are invited to submit articles for publication, with a deadline of the 10th of each month for inclusion in the following month's issue. Submission details and contact information for Lew Kurtz are provided.

articles.title: COMET COMMENTS, Feb. 2, 1996
articles.summary: This "Comet Comments" update from February 1996 announces the recent discovery of three new comets by amateur astronomers: Jedicke, Szczepanski, and Hyakutake. It particularly highlights Comet Hyakutake (C/1996 B2) as an upcoming naked-eye object in March and April, suitable for public viewing, while also noting Comet Hale-Bopp's brighter-than-expected reappearance, making four comets visible in binoculars. The report provides observational details, projected brightness, and visibility predictions for each of the newly found comets.

articles.title: EPHEMERIDES
articles.summary: This document provides detailed ephemeris data for four comets: C/1995 Y1 (Hyakutaka), C/1996 B1 (Szczepanski), C/1996 B2 (Hyakutake), and C/1995 O1 (Hale-Bopp), primarily for observing periods in March 1996. It lists their celestial coordinates (Right Ascension, Declination), elongation from the Sun, and estimated visual magnitudes for specific dates. Additionally, a table of key orbital elements such as perihelion date, distance, inclination, and eccentricity is included for each comet.
